title: The held world, walkable - and is this the right frame?
question: Two thirds of this picture is underground. In the sandbox that is right because you dig; here you never will. Should the camera sit higher, so a walk is mostly sky and canopy?
context_md:
`cargo run --release --bin druid` now runs. Both panes are the same game, same size (2560x960, five screens across), same 8,000 frames of growing before the world is held - they differ only in the worldgen preset.

- **rolling** is the sandbox's shipped default: a world built so you can tunnel into it
- **druid** is a new preset for growing things - the screen-high rock walls cut right down, twice the soil depth, soil kept on steeper ground, no caves, no buried lenses, wetter, and more life scattered

**What I already measured, so you do not have to judge it by eye:** the druid preset more than doubles what grows. That part is settled and is not what the card is asking.

**What I am unsure of, and it applies to both panes.** The camera follows the gnome and shows 320 rows of a 960-row world, so most of the frame is a cutaway of rock strata under his feet. It is faithful, and I think it may be wrong for this game - but raising the camera is a taste call and I would rather not guess it.

**Please ignore:** there is no rim yet, the world is held but nothing marks where your carried circle is, and the trees are whatever 8,000 frames produced rather than anything tuned.
